messages:
noah: heads-up — hit a weird redaction leak in the Go quickstart during onboarding. With LOG_LEVEL=debug the request-id shows up in zap's debug lines but is redacted at info.

sara: can you paste the quick repro and a log snippet?

noah: repro: clone github.com/redwood/sample-apps/go-telemetry, CONFIG=dev LOG_LEVEL=debug go run ./cmd/server, POST /auth. Logs: 
```
DEBUG server: parsed token fields request_id=tmp-42
DEBUG zap/http: incoming request - request_id=tmp-42
INFO app.handlers: login.success - request_id=REDACTED
```
When LOG_LEVEL=info the debug lines vanish and everything looks redacted.

ethan: interesting. Go's zap often adds fields at logger creation time (logger = logger.With(zap.String("request_id", rid))). If middleware binds request_id into a context-aware logger after zap's handler is already used by the HTTP server, debug path from net/http or other libs can log before redaction.

noah: exactly. In the quickstart the redaction filter is installed as a zapcore.Core wrapper during telemetry.Init(), but in dev mode we start a dev HTTP server that constructs its own logger earlier. On debug builds the server emits extra debug lines before telemetry.Init() runs.

sara: two options: 1) make telemetry.Init() register a global safe redaction core synchronously (and document that Init should run before server start), or 2) provide a helper AttachRedactionToLogger(logger) that users can call on their server logger.

ethan: +1 on both. For Go we should also add a tiny helper that scans common packages' loggers (http.DefaultServeMux logger wrappers) and attach the redaction core if possible. But reflect-heavy code is awkward — better to provide clear onboarding guidance and an easy Attach helper.

noah: I pushed a tiny repro branch and a patch that calls telemetry.Init() at the top of main.go before any server/handler setup and it fixes the leak. I'll open a PR to change the quickstart and add a comment in README about init order.

sara: also add a CI smoke test: run the server with LOG_LEVEL=debug in a subprocess, hit /auth, and assert the captured logs contain no unredacted tokens or request ids. Keep the test robust by retrying startup.

docs-bot: Draft docs change created: docs/telemetry/init-order.md — "Run telemetry.Init() before creating server loggers or middleware that may expose context fields."

telemetry-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1776 — "Go quickstart: debug log path can expose request_id before redaction; recommend Init before server creation". Labels: devex, telemetry, bug.

ethan: nice. For backward compatibility we should also add a short note in the SDK release notes and consider making AttachRedactionToLogger() exported in the next minor.

noah: will link the PR and the CI test in the issue. thanks all :thumbsup:

sara: adding a follow-up: check Dedicated/private builds where init hooks might be delayed by sidecar startup ordering. We'll add a checklist item to the Dedicated onboarding doc.

noah: logging follow-up noted, will try to reproduce in a Dedicated staging pool tomorrow and update the issue.
